landing.faq.description: Everything you need to know before getting started.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.
landing.cta.headline: Ready to ship your SaaS?
landing.cta.subheadline: Stop wiring auth, payments, and RBAC from scratch. Start with ShipAny Next and build what actually makes your product unique.

qwen.guide.heading: A practical guide to Qwen Image 2.1
qwen.guide.intro.one: Qwen Image 2.1 is a model from the Qwen team that brings text-to-image creation and image editing into one image workflow. Its official release describes a 7B visual generation component, native transparent RGBA images, support for multiple reference images and refined text and portrait details. Those are capabilities of the model itself. QwenImage AI is an independent space for exploring these possibilities and generating images through a configured model service.
qwen.guide.intro.two: Before choosing a tool, decide whether you need a new scene, a revision of an existing image, a transparent asset, or a composition guided by references. The sections below turn those choices into a brief. In the studio, signed-in users can submit text-to-image prompts to the configured Qwen Image service.
qwen.guide.1.heading: Start with a clear text-to-image brief
qwen.guide.1.one: For a new image, write the subject first, then describe the setting, viewpoint, composition and light. “A ceramic cup” leaves almost every visual choice open. “A handmade ceramic cup on a pale stone table, viewed from above in soft morning light” gives the model a coherent scene. Add mood and materials when they matter. A useful prompt reads like compact art direction, not a pile of unrelated style tags.
qwen.guide.1.two: Choose a frame with the concept: square for a product, portrait for a character, wide for a landscape. The official repository lists recommended 2K sizes. The studio sends your selected ratio with the generation request.
qwen.guide.2.heading: Describe edits in terms of change and continuity
qwen.guide.2.one: The model supports editing as well as creation. Name the area or object to change, then state what must stay. For example: replace a grey sky with a warm sunset while preserving the building, camera angle and people. This separates the requested change from elements that already work. For a product image, mention color, label and silhouette when brand consistency matters.
qwen.guide.2.two: The model also supports marked regions, masks and multiple references. In the studio, you can preview one image locally and draft an edit instruction; editing is not connected to the generation endpoint yet. Copy the wording to a compatible editing tool when ready.
qwen.guide.3.heading: Plan transparent assets and layered ideas
qwen.guide.3.one: Native transparency is a distinctive feature of the release. Qwen says the model can create or edit RGBA images and extract a subject from a photograph as a transparent layer. That makes it relevant to stickers, product cutouts, icons and compositing work. If transparency is essential, request it plainly and describe the subject’s edges, material and pose. The official repository provides an explicit RGBA prompt pattern.
qwen.guide.3.two: Ask for a complete subject, specify shadows, and check how details read on light and dark backgrounds. A sticker may need a clean silhouette; a product cutout may need exact packaging text. Verify the alpha channel in your model tool.
qwen.guide.4.heading: Use references without losing the main idea
qwen.guide.4.one: Qwen’s documentation describes up to ten reference images for multi-subject composition and editing. References can convey a person, product, clothing, location or visual language. Give each image a job: reference one for the subject, reference two for the outfit, reference three for the setting. Then describe the new scene in one sentence. This gives the model a hierarchy instead of blending everything without direction.
qwen.guide.4.two: Specify which face, shape, logo or color should remain. This studio previews one local reference for an editing draft; it is not a ten-image uploader. The gallery is original site illustration, not output from your prompt.
qwen.guide.5.heading: Make text, layout and review part of the prompt
qwen.guide.5.one: Qwen highlights improved typography and detail in its newest release. For a poster, label or sign, put the exact words in quotation marks and state placement, scale and language. Describe the hierarchy: headline first, supporting line second, image third. For an editorial visual, describe the light and texture that matter most, such as soft window light or crisp paper grain, without conflicting adjectives.
qwen.guide.5.two: When a generation endpoint is configured, check spelling, hands, product details and composition in the result. Revise one constraint at a time. The studio submits generation prompts and displays the returned image; exact results depend on the model service.
qwen.guide.faq.heading: Qwen Image 2.1 questions
qwen.guide.faq.1.question: Can I generate a Qwen Image 2.1 image on this site?
qwen.guide.faq.1.answer: Yes, when the site operator has configured the model service. Sign in, enter a prompt, choose an aspect ratio and submit it from the playground. The gallery illustrations remain original site artwork, separate from generated results.
qwen.guide.faq.2.question: What can Qwen Image 2.1 do?
qwen.guide.faq.2.answer: According to Qwen’s official repository, the model combines text-to-image generation and image editing. It supports transparent RGBA output, multi-reference editing and local edit guidance, with improved typography and visual detail. Availability and exact controls depend on the implementation you use.
qwen.guide.faq.3.question: Are the gallery images Qwen Image 2.1 results?
qwen.guide.faq.3.answer: No. They are original illustrative studies for this website. They are not generated from your prompt and should not be read as a benchmark or a claim about what the model will produce.
qwen.guide.faq.4.question: How should I write a better image editing prompt?
qwen.guide.faq.4.answer: Describe the requested change, identify the region or object involved, and list the details that must remain. Include reference roles and exact text when relevant. Test the prompt in a connected model tool and revise based on the result.
